html:
King of Kongo from about 1509 to his death around 1542, born Mvemba a Nzinga. He was baptised with his father in 1491, when the Kongo king accepted Christianity, and won the throne after a fight with a half-brother.

He made the Catholic Church the state religion, built churches in his capital Mbanza Kongo, and sent young nobles to study in Lisbon. His son Henrique became a bishop in 1518, the first from sub-Saharan Africa.

Afonso wanted Portuguese priests, teachers and craftsmen, but Portuguese traders wanted slaves. In 1526 he wrote to King João III of Portugal that merchants were seizing free people, even nobles, and that the slave trade was emptying his land. He did not stop the trade, but he tried to control it. His letters are among the earliest African writings about the trade that survive.
